## Without Validation, We're Groping in the Dark

::: {.fragment .fade-in-then-semi-out fragment-index=1}
> "All quantitative models of language are **wrong** — but some are **useful**" <br>
>
> [@grimmerTextDataPromise2013, p. 269]
:::

<br>

::: {.fragment fragment-index=2}
> "The use of computers in content analysis invokes a shift in **methodological emphasis**, from solving the **human problem** of achieving **reliable coding** for large volumes of text [...] to solving the **computational problem** of **preserving relevant readings** of the texts."
>
> [@krippendorffContentAnalysisIntroduction2018, p. 215]
:::

::: {.column width="48%"}
::: {.fragment .fade-in-then-semi-out fragment-index=5}
In **manual content analysis**, we care about **reliability**:

::: {.small-text}
- **Inter-coder reliability**: do coders equally apply the coding rules at t1?
- **Intra-coder reliability**: does coder A apply the coding rules equally at t1 and t2?
- **Coder–researcher reliability**: do coders apply coding rules like the researcher?
:::
:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index=6}
In **automated content analysis**, we care mostly about **validity**:

::: {.small-text}
- **Semantic validity** (model–researcher reliability): does the model apply coding rules like the researcher / preserve meaning? → tested by comparing model outcomes with a *gold standard*
- **Criterion validity**: does the model outcome correlate with external measures? → tested by correlating model outcomes with *self-reports* or *self-assigned labels*
:::
:::
:::

:::

## Coding a Gold Standard

::: {.incremental}
- Manually coding a *smaller-ish* amount of text with high reliability
- Testing semantic validity by comparing model outcomes against this "ground truth"
- Assumption: "*if trained correctly*, humans will make the most correct and valid classifications of texts" [@songValidationsWeTrust2020, p. 551]
- Because humans interpret rules differently, establishing a ground truth typically requires:
  - a **detailed, crystal-clear codebook** (e.g., <https://osf.io/2z3dk/>)
  - many rounds of **coder training** and **reliability testing**
  - **multiple independent codings** of the same material, with the final code determined by majority vote
:::

::: {.fragment}
::: {.callout-caution}
## Suggestions by @songValidationsWeTrust2020 for a gold standard
- Improve inter-coder reliability as much as possible (ideally Krippendorff's α ≥ .70, or even ≥ .90)
- Use large validation samples (min. 1,300 cases if inter-coder reliability is α ≥ .70)
- Proper training is required to avoid coder drift (i.e., low intra-coder reliability)
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## Want to know more about improving reliability in human codings?
@krippendorffContentAnalysisIntroduction2018; @neuendorfContentAnalysisGuidebook2017; @roesslerInhaltsanalyse2017 [German]
:::

## Typical Key Metrics {auto-animate="true"}

::: {.incremental}
- When comparing categories measured on numeric scales [(e.g., a sentiment scale from −3 to +3)]{.small-text}:<br>Pearson or rank correlation
- When comparing categories measured as dummy variables [(e.g., present vs. not present)]{.small-text}:<br>Recall, Precision, F1, and Accuracy [(or more advanced reliability coefficients, like Kappa or Krippendorff's α)]{.small-text}
:::

<br>

::: {.columns}

::: {.column .fragment width="42%"}

<br>Confusion Matrix:

<table class="confusion" data-id="confusion">
<tr>
<td class="cm-corner"></td><td class="cm-corner"></td>
<td class="cm-colhead" colspan="2">**Model Classification**</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="cm-corner"></td><td class="cm-corner"></td>
<td class="cm-colkey">1</td><td class="cm-colkey">0</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="cm-rowhead" rowspan="2">Gold-<br>Standard</td>
<td class="cm-rowkey">1</td>
<td class="cm-cell">True Positive<br>(TP)</td>
<td class="cm-cell">False Negative<br>(FN)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="cm-rowkey">0</td>
<td class="cm-cell">False Positive<br>(FP)</td>
<td class="cm-cell">True Negative<br>(TN)</td>
</tr>
</table>
:::

::: {.column width="58%"}
<div data-id="metrics-formulas">
<div class="fragment">$$Precision = \dfrac{TP}{TP + FP}$$</div>
<div class="fragment">$$Recall = \dfrac{TP}{TP + FN}$$</div>
<div class="fragment">$$Accuracy = \dfrac{TP + TN}{TP + TN + FP + FN}$$</div>
<div class="fragment">$$F1 = \dfrac{2 \times Precision \times Recall}{Precision + Recall}$$</div>
</div>
:::

:::
